features.note: amphitheater used for the leaders' meeting and the weekly troop campfire
archery badge plus open archery periods
showerhouse near each campsite
chapel overlooking one of the camp lakes
climbing offered alongside the COPE program
high COPE course thirty feet off the ground
cinematography taught in the handicraft area
first-year camper track covering Tenderfoot through First Class requirements
fishing from rowboats, docks, or shore, with a fly fishing badge offered
basketry and wood carving through to cinematography
ecology and conservation area focused on observing and documenting nature
midweek overnight adventures run out of the first-year and outdoor skills areas
units can choose patrol or in-site cooking instead of dining hall service
a pavilion with picnic tables in every campsite, plus one at the dining hall
four-person tent cabins with wooden floors, screens, canvas walls, rigid roofs, and cots
Scouts whose unit is not attending can come with a provisional unit
rifle badge plus open rifle periods
every campsite has its own dock and rowboat with direct lake access
shotgun badge plus open shotgun periods
parade ground used for camp-wide games such as soccer and ultimate frisbee
space exploration and game design badges
open swim during free time
two waterfront areas on separate lakes, one of them a marina
wood carving in the handicraft area
five-hundred-foot zip line
